title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a differentiable manifold (the interesting case is dim 2, e.g. a Riemann surface near a puncture) and x is a point of X. Two objects are attached to x.

- D_x^* is the germ at x of the punctured neighbourhood X \ {x}.
- $_x (S_x) is the 'sphere of half-tangents' at x, that is (T_xX \ 0)/R_{>0}.

On the previous page Grothendieck takes a differentiable arc germ (branch) γ issuing from x, with half-tangent Δ = Δ(γ). He uses γ as a 'base point at infinity' of D_x^* and defines a pointed universal covering D^{*~}_{x,γ} = Revuniv(D_x^*, γ). He identifies it with Θ(Δ) via the inclusions γ ⊂ {Δ}^~ ⊂ D_x^*. Comparing two arcs γ, γ' then gives the bijection (80): Isom(γ,γ') ≅ Isom_{Π1($_x)}(Δ,Δ').

This page states the summary diagram (93) of equivalences of groupoids:
- Top row: germ.diff(X,x) → Π_1($_x), γ ↦ Δ(γ).
- Left column: γ ↦ Revuniv(D_x^*, γ), landing in Revuniv(D_x^*), the groupoid of universal coverings of D_x^*.
- Right column: a ↦ Revuniv($_x, a), landing in Revuniv($_x).
- Bottom row: Revuniv(D_x^*) ≅ Revuniv($_x).
- Diagonal: Θ : Π_1($_x) → Revuniv(D_x^*), the key equivalence (81).

The marginal note explains the difficulty: there is no direct, chart-free map linking D_x^* and the space $_x. Hence the only a priori explicit functor (94) Revuniv(D_x^*) → Revuniv($_x) is the composite of Θ^{-1} with the canonical functor Π_1($_x) → Revuniv($_x).

Grothendieck concludes that in this 'differential topological geometry' the key construction is Θ, which he has taken pains to define invariantly. When a local isomorphism (90) f : (T_xX, 0) → (X, x) is given, Θ becomes a canonical construction inside a vector space V: a half-line Δ in V gives an arc germ, hence a universal covering of V \ 0 pointed at Δ. The next page discusses how this depends continuously on Δ, and the functoriality under diffeomorphisms fixing x and differentiable at x.

Purpose: to give a topological/differentiable foundation for 'tangential' base points, i.e. base points at a puncture given by directions. These are needed for local monodromy and fundamental groupoids of curves at their punctures in the Teichmüller/Galois (Longue Marche) programme.
errors: No error, but a gap the author himself flags: no direct map D_x^* → $_x. In the C^1 setting the real oriented blow-up of X at x supplies exactly this canonical link. Its exceptional boundary is $_x, and D_x^* together with $_x is a collar, so both include into the blow-up germ as homotopy equivalences. This would make Θ immediate and chart-free.
In dimension ≥ 3, $_x is simply connected and the whole construction degenerates; it has content only in dimension 2 (and for 1 the sphere is two points). The page does not restrict the dimension.

ideas.what: Using germs of differentiable arcs at x (equivalently their half-tangents) as base points 'at infinity' for the punctured neighbourhood germ D_x^*, with isomorphisms between such base points given by isomorphisms of pointed universal coverings.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); also Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in La Longue Marche (1981) / Esquisse (1984) discussion of base points for Teichmüller groupoids; unsure

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids germ.diff(X,x) ≃ Π_1($_x) ≃ Revuniv(D_x^*) ≃ Revuniv($_x) via the functor Θ.
ideas.modern_name: homotopy equivalence of the punctured neighbourhood with the boundary of the real oriented blow-up (link of a point)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (A'Campo; Kato–Nakayama in log geometry for the algebraic analogue)

ideas.what: Insistence on a chart-free, invariant definition of Θ, functorial for homeomorphisms that fix x and are differentiable at x; with a chart, it reduces to a homogeneous construction in a vector space.
ideas.modern_name: naturality of the real blow-up / unit tangent sphere bundle

missed.claim: A careful, invariant topological-differential foundation for tangential base points (arcs/half-tangents as base points, groupoid equivalence with Π_1 of the sphere of directions). It appears in Grothendieck's sequel to the Longue Marche, which may predate Deligne's 1989 formalism. This is mainly historical priority, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: Finalement, dans ces considérations de géométrie topologique différentielle, la construction-clef est celle du foncteur Θ (81). Nous avons pris quelque peine à la définir de façon invariante.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the genesis of tangential base points in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. The mathematics itself is now standard via the real oriented blow-up.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard local topology (link of a point, real blow-up) organised as a groupoid version of tangential base points. It is of modest historical interest if it predates Deligne, but there is no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'Revêtements(D^*_x,γ)' and similar should read 'Revuniv(...)' (universal coverings), consistent with the previous page.
Marginal note reads roughly: 'Bien sûr, la difficulté ici provient du fait qu'on ne connaissait pas de façon directe [?] de lien [?] entre D_x^* et l'espace $_x ...'; partially illegible.
'Le seul foncteur qui soit par avance rendu explicite' is probably 'Le seul foncteur qui était par avance explicité'.
(90) is a local isomorphism f : (T_x(X), 0) → (X, x) from the tangent space.
